account: So far today the town seems quiet. During my morning market walk, Townsfolk 28 and 18 both told me that the baker had been carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That sounds consistent with ordinary bread-making; I have no evidence that it serves another purpose. The other residents I asked at the plaza and inn had no news. My secretary also said she had received no correspondence or town news. The one curious detail is my appointment for tea at fifteen hundred with 'the neighbour' at an east-bank dockside cottage: the appointment book names neither the host nor the precise cottage. The secretary did not know either, and I asked her to confirm the details. It could simply be an incompletely recorded social appointment, not evidence of anything secret. I still have a feeling that something may be happening without my knowledge, but nothing I have seen or heard identifies a hidden activity, its participants, or its purpose. I have finished the market walk and reached home ahead of noon lunch; my next scheduled business is town accounts at thirteen hundred.
